newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: W&H, INL star as NZ shares close higher.
newsitem.headline: W&H, INL star as NZ shares close higher.

text.p: * NZ shares stronger on takeover activity, higher Wall St
* Analysts see Independent's Wilson & Horton bid as too low
* INL rises in sympathy with W&H, market leaders firm ---------------------------(Sept 17)---------------------------- Price movements at close
365 nil * Volume $47 million. Futures up 13 at 1,134
Takeover target Wilson and Horton and fellow-publisher INL were the star performers as New Zealand shares closed higher on Tuesday.

Wilson and Horton gained NZ$1.05 or 10.8 percent to $10.75 on modest volume of 73,932 shares as analysts took the view that a $10.50/share offer from Irish-based Independent Newspapers Plc may be too low.

"You've got a few retail people getting out, happy with the price they can get now, rather than waiting. But having said that, I think a lot of institutional investors and larger holders will wait out," said Duncan Rutherford at ANZ

"It's a story that's going to take a bit of time unfolding," said Don Turkington of Cavill White Securities. "There's certainly plenty of buying above the bid price and people will be just weighing up what their chances are of getting even more."

Wilson and Horton's board meets on Wednesday and will commission an independent appraisal before Independent launches its written and on-market offer early next month. Rutherford said he expected further scrappy trade in the meantime.
INL, the only other major media stock, gained in sympathy to close 35 cents higher at $5.90.

Telecom, back in favour after falls last week, ended eight cents higher after a similar rise on Monday. The Fletcher Challenge "letter" stocks all climbed, with heavy volume of 2.85 million in Fletcher Building, up two cents to $3.31.
